## Component template library

- [templates list](#templates-list) — List and filter the canonical component-template library.
- [templates search](#templates-search) — Search component templates by identity, purpose or capability.
- [templates show](#templates-show) — Inspect one complete component-template JSON definition.
- [templates tree](#templates-tree) — Inspect the resolved Atomic Design child composition of one template.
- [templates validate](#templates-validate) — Validate one template or the complete installed component-template catalog.
- [templates schema](#templates-schema) — Print the versioned component-template JSON Schema.
- [templates coverage](#templates-coverage) — Inspect Atomic Design, category, documentation and composition coverage.
- [templates docs](#templates-docs) — Plan deterministic Markdown documentation generated from component-template JSON; replaces only its receipted, unedited output.
- [templates instantiate](#templates-instantiate) — Plan adding a component or page template to the canonical Companion project model.

## Prototype versions and variants

- [prototypes list](#prototypes-list) — Read prototypes, versions, variants and the single pinned generator selection.
- [prototypes compare](#prototypes-compare) — Read complete snapshot differences without changing saved content or activation.
- [prototypes prototype-details](#prototypes-prototype-details) — Edit prototype display details without changing folder slugs or saved designs.
- [prototypes version-details](#prototypes-version-details) — Edit the label of an unsealed version without changing saved designs.
- [prototypes restore-snapshot](#prototypes-restore-snapshot) — Restore a saved reference into an editable draft, retaining its previous content in a sealed recovery version.
- [prototypes create](#prototypes-create) — Capture a complete project as docs/concepts/&lt;slug&gt;/, version v1, draft variant main.
- [prototypes version](#prototypes-version) — Copy a saved version into a new editable version; all copied variants start as drafts.
- [prototypes fork](#prototypes-fork) — Fork the selected saved variant; edits never change the original.
- [prototypes save](#prototypes-save) — Save complete project JSON to a draft in an unsealed version.
- [prototypes details](#prototypes-details) — Maintain a draft variant name and hypothesis without changing its path.
- [prototypes status](#prototypes-status) — Set draft, review, approved or archived status; activation is a separate operation.
- [prototypes activate](#prototypes-activate) — Pin an approved variant for generation and demote any previous active variant.
- [prototypes deactivate](#prototypes-deactivate) — Clear the generator selection without deleting snapshots.
- [prototypes seal](#prototypes-seal) — Seal snapshot content in a version; create a new version for further edits.
- [prototypes archive](#prototypes-archive) — Archive an inactive prototype without deleting any of its files.
- [prototypes restore](#prototypes-restore) — Restore an archived prototype without activating it.
- [prototypes import](#prototypes-import) — Import a validated workspace bundle using reviewed, conflict-checked file writes.
- [prototypes export](#prototypes-export) — Export the complete workspace to inert JSON outside docs/concepts; never overwrite different files.
- [prototypes adopt](#prototypes-adopt) — Import the pinned active project through the existing configuration conflict workflow.
- [prototypes generate](#prototypes-generate) — Generate strictly from the saved active variant; no implicit selection or process execution.

## External project starters

- [starters list](#starters-list) — Discover project-local JSON starters; no bundled fallback.
- [starters show](#starters-show) — Inspect one complete editable starter definition and its processes.
- [starters validate](#starters-validate) — Validate one or all installed definitions without writes or execution.
- [starters schema](#starters-schema) — Print the versioned starter-definition JSON Schema.
- [starters add](#starters-add) — Plan adding one JSON definition; never executes processes.
- [starters edit](#starters-edit) — Plan replacing one definition from validated JSON.
- [starters run](#starters-run) — Review/explicitly execute processes from a generated project receipt.
- [starters pack](#starters-pack) — Create the standalone starter-definition ZIP, separate from the shell.
- [starters coverage](#starters-coverage) — Inspect source-derived visual model coverage and explicit interaction gaps; never a native acceptance claim.

## Generated UI progress and evidence

- [ui status](#ui-status) — Report UI implementation progress per surface, interaction and journey from generated files; static analysis only, never an acceptance claim.
- [ui gallery](#ui-gallery) — Capture a screenshot gallery (surface x state x scenario x theme x width) with index.json and gallery.html for human review; never acceptance or a baseline.

## Product-trio handout

- [handout generate](#handout-generate) — Review create-only generation of the root product-trio handout; never overwrites answers or runs processes.
- [handout refresh](#handout-refresh) — Review source-fingerprint refresh while preserving answers and notes and resetting review checkboxes.
- [handout validate](#handout-validate) — Validate required handout decisions and source freshness without writes or execution authorization.
- [handout inspect](#handout-inspect) — Read structured handout answers, diagnostics and non-authorizing readiness.

## Start a project

- [new](#new) — Create a new project in &lt;dir&gt; from a reviewed file or Companion starter, or an exported companion project (--from); previews unless --yes. Project starters run without &lt;dir&gt;: new --starter &lt;id&gt;.
- [setup](#setup) — Configure this folder from a verified starter, blank project or JSON; no implicit install.
- [setup status](#setup-status) — Inspect resumable setup progress against actual current input bytes; no processes or writes.
- [setup resume](#setup-resume) — Explicitly run one setup stage with fresh input checks and retained interruption/failure history.
- [project inspect](#project-inspect) — Validate a companion export and report compiler obligations.
- [project import](#project-import) — Review configuration conflicts and accept a design snapshot.
- [project schema](#project-schema) — Discover the versioned project-v6 transport schema and semantic validation boundary.
- [project validate](#project-validate) — Validate complete project v6 JSON without generation or writes; no authored content in reports.
- [project measure](#project-measure) — Measure bounded model import/export, projection and arrangement locally; no UI or native qualification.
- [generate](#generate) — Plan generation for the configured project in place.
- [concept schema](#concept-schema) — Discover the data-only concept manifest contract.
- [concept inspect](#concept-inspect) — Inspect a docs/concepts JSON/HTML input, or return the current project base hash.
- [concept import](#concept-import) — Plan reviewed project, new-feature or base-bound improvement intake. Never executes HTML/source.

## Adopt an existing project

- [adopt analyze](#adopt-analyze) — Analyze an existing project read-only (bounded, no code executed) and report its stack, tooling and Workbench compatibility findings.
- [adopt plan](#adopt-plan) — Render the analysis as a Markdown integration plan; previews with its SHA-256 and writes one file only after --yes or --apply.
- [adopt skill](#adopt-skill) — Install the adopt-existing-project agent skill (Claude and Codex copies) into the target; never overwrites a different file.

## Develop and check

- [install](#install) — Explicit exact-lock npm ci; reviewed lifecycle hooks may run.
- [dev](#dev) — Run development watch, UI harness or the real-Obsidian sandbox; cancel with Ctrl-C.
- [build](#build) — Run the existing production bundler.
- [clickdummy build](#clickdummy-build) — Build the generated Vue project as offline HTML with synthetic read data. No native/business writes.
- [test](#test) — Run unit/project, browser, native qualification or real-Obsidian tests.
- [check](#check) — Fast daily/agent gate: typecheck, lint and tests; runs every step and summarizes failures. --fast narrows it to a diff (--base &lt;ref&gt;); --plan lists the gates a diff requires. Not verify.
- [check submission](#check-submission) — Local mirror of documented Obsidian community review rules; runs the project ESLint configuration (trusted project code) and writes nothing.
- [ci](#ci) — Reproduce GitHub Actions jobs locally: list workflows/jobs, print a job's exact shell commands (dry run) or run its run: steps with --execute.
- [make](#make) — Use the shared maker registry and file planner.
- [entities check](#entities-check) — Validate the explicitly registered entity definitions with the installed Vite toolchain; writes nothing.
- [entities catalog](#entities-catalog) — Print the source-derived entity catalog (backend, schema, fields, defaults, Markdown mappings); writes nothing.
- [styles inspect](#styles-inspect) — Validate saved design tokens and inspect scoped Nuxt UI bindings.
- [styles export](#styles-export) — Plan deterministic CSS, JSON, Markdown or HTML exports.

## Application documentation

- [docs import](#docs-import) — Review typed Markdown files/folders into actual project elements without deleting absent data.
- [docs export](#docs-export) — Generate complete, lossless application Markdown documentation with conflict protection.
- [docs validate](#docs-validate) — Validate typed documentation and native model references without writing.
- [docs status](#docs-status) — Inspect documentation drift, missing bindings and export coverage without writing.
- [docs schema](#docs-schema) — Discover typed Markdown fields and ownership rules without reading a project.
- [docs recover](#docs-recover) — Review or explicitly roll back an interrupted documentation operation; never overwrite intervening edits.

## Optional Obsidian CLI

- [obsidian status](#obsidian-status) — Verify the official Obsidian CLI (1.12.7+) and inspect one explicitly selected vault.
- [obsidian files](#obsidian-files) — List Markdown files in one explicitly selected vault; never falls back to the active vault.
- [obsidian read](#obsidian-read) — Read one non-hidden Markdown file from the explicitly selected vault.
- [obsidian prepare](#obsidian-prepare) — Scan configured documentation paths through the official CLI and propose existing reviewed docs-import commands.

## Optional Storybook

- [storybook status](#storybook-status) — Inspect the independent story-generation and optional Storybook switches; never installs.
- [storybook install](#storybook-install) — Explicitly install the enabled optional Storybook workspace; first resolution then exact-lock npm ci.
- [storybook check](#storybook-check) — Type-check the installed optional Storybook workspace; not a default project gate.
- [storybook dev](#storybook-dev) — Run the enabled optional Storybook locally; no auto-open, telemetry or cloud publication.
- [storybook build](#storybook-build) — Build the enabled optional Storybook to local static files; never publishes.

## Optional Airship

- [airship status](#airship-status) — Read optional Airship configuration and local install state.
- [airship enable](#airship-enable) — Review enabling local safe Airship tooling; never installs or launches.
- [airship disable](#airship-disable) — Review disabling future Airship launches; preserve installed tooling and edits.
- [airship install](#airship-install) — Explicitly install the pinned CLI in an isolated project-local prefix (--yes).
- [airship start](#airship-start) — Explicitly start the local safe editor against the source preview (--yes).
- [airship doctor](#airship-doctor) — Run third-party Airship diagnostics only with --yes.

## Optional local agent MCP

- [mcp](#mcp) — Start the project-local stdio MCP bridge; setup must opt in and client trust/approval stays external.

## Project compiler

- [compiler check](#compiler-check) — Analyze project JSON without generation or writes; --report-dir explicitly retains diagnostics.
- [compiler inspect](#compiler-inspect) — Inspect normalized IR or an in-memory artifact inventory; never applies a workspace plan.
- [compiler explain](#compiler-explain) — Explain a stable compiler diagnostic code.

## Reviewed plans

- [plan inspect](#plan-inspect) — Rebuild and compare a saved request plan; never execute it.
- [plan apply](#plan-apply) — Rebuild a saved request and apply only its matching reviewed plan.

## Inspect/configure

- [status](#status) — Project identity, configuration and readiness observations.
- [doctor](#doctor) — Read-only toolchain/configuration diagnostics.
- [support report](#support-report) — Collect an opt-in, allowlisted local support report without identities, paths, content or network calls.
- [version](#version) — Report the pinned framework and current Node versions.
- [config get](#config-get) — Read the effective configuration.
- [config explain](#config-explain) — Explain persisted configuration and identity authority.
- [config validate](#config-validate) — Validate configuration without changes.
- [config set](#config-set) — Plan a validated configuration update from JSON.

## Test vault and data

- [vault prepare](#vault-prepare) — Plan a marker in the configured isolated test vault.
- [plugin install](#plugin-install) — Install exact built assets into the approved test vault; never enable.
- [data plan](#data-plan) — Shared owned test-data plan; never touches production sources.
- [data apply](#data-apply) — Shared owned test-data apply; never touches production sources.
- [data reset-plan](#data-reset-plan) — Shared owned test-data reset-plan; never touches production sources.
- [data reset](#data-reset) — Shared owned test-data reset; never touches production sources.

## Discovery (agents)

- [help](#help) — Discover commands without reading project code; --all lists every command.
- [capabilities](#capabilities) — Versioned command and maker contracts; no custom-code discovery.
- [schema](#schema) — Machine-readable operation request/result contracts.

## Maintainers

- [verify](#verify) — Run existing full verification; project scope is explicitly separate.
- [framework status](#framework-status) — Inspect the pinned kit and its integrity.
- [framework pack](#framework-pack) — Build a deterministic compiled developer-kit ZIP locally.
- [framework upgrade](#framework-upgrade) — Plan an explicit kit replacement; deletes only verified retired kit files and keeps edited plugin configs or reports a conflict.
- [release prepare](#release-prepare) — Plan source version and release-note changes.
- [release check](#release-check) — Inspect packaging and optionally validate a retained release plan.
- [release rehearse](#release-rehearse) — Run existing fixed-candidate rehearsal; no public promotion.
- [release operate](#release-operate) — Use the existing guarded release executor and separate authorization.

## templates list

List and filter the canonical component-template library.

```sh
node bin/app templates list [options]
```

**Effect:** read. Inspection/discovery. Some commands write reports only when explicitly requested; inspect command-specific help.

**Maximum positional arguments:** 0. See usage and examples for their meaning; this bound does not mean all arguments are optional.

| Option | Kind | Meaning | Values / default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| --type | value | Component-template type filter. | Values: component, component-with-children, page, page-with-bricks |
| --atomic-level | value | Atomic Design level filter. | Values: atom, molecule, organism, template, page |
| --category | value | Exact component-template category filter. | See command semantics |
| --tag | value | Exact component-template tag filter. | See command semantics |
| --for | value | Application archetype recommendation filter, for example editor or obsidian-plugin. | See command semantics |
| --json | flag | Print exactly one versioned JSON result on stdout. | See command semantics |
| --root | value | Project folder to operate on. | Default: nearest folder with shell.config.json or bin/app |
| --no-interaction | flag | Never prompt, even on a TTY. | See command semantics |
| --help | flag | Describe this command instead of running it. | See command semantics |

Parser-accepted common flags without documented semantics here: `--apply`, `--dry-run`, `--plan-out`, `--timeout`, `--yes`. Do not rely on them to prevent or authorize effects.

### Examples

```sh

node bin/app templates list --for editor --json
```
